questions.q: What problem does a transaction solve?
options: Duplicate rows in a table
A multi-step change failing halfway through, leaving data in an inconsistent state
Slow query performance
Incorrect column data types
questions.explain: Without a transaction, one statement succeeding and the next failing can leave data corrupted (like stock vanishing between locations).

options: Marks the start of a group of statements that must all succeed together
Deletes all uncommitted changes
Creates a new database
Immediately saves all pending changes permanently
questions.explain: It opens a transaction boundary — nothing inside it is permanent until COMMIT.

options: Starts a new transaction
Only saves the first statement in the transaction
Makes every change made since BEGIN TRANSACTION permanent, all at once
Undoes every change since BEGIN TRANSACTION
questions.explain: COMMIT is what finalizes the transaction's changes as permanent.

options: Undoes every change made since the matching BEGIN TRANSACTION, as if none of it happened
Restarts the transaction from the beginning
Makes the changes permanent, same as COMMIT
Only undoes the most recent statement, not the whole transaction
questions.explain: ROLLBACK is the safety net that prevents a half-finished multi-step change from corrupting data.

questions.q: Before COMMIT runs, are the transaction's changes visible outside the current session?
options: No — they are provisional, visible within the session but not yet permanently saved
This depends entirely on the table's data type
Changes are never visible until the server restarts
Yes, they are immediately visible and permanent to everyone
questions.explain: Changes inside an open transaction remain provisional until COMMIT finalizes them.
